chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Sabbah al-Hazza', from Abu al-Tayyar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I had some capital, but it dispersed, and I felt severe distress because of it.' He said to me, 'Do you have a shop in the market?' I said, 'Yes, and I have left it.' He said, 'When you return to Kufa, sit in your shop and sweep it. And when you intend to go out to your market, pray two or four rak'ahs. Then, after your prayer, say: I turn to You with no power of my own and no strength, but with Your power, O Lord, and Your strength. I disclaim all power and strength except through You, for You are my power and from You comes my strength. O God, grant me from Your vast bounty a plentiful, good provision, while I am humble in Your health/well-being, for no one else possesses it.'
He said: 'So I did that, and I would go out to my shop until I feared that the tax collector would take the rent of my shop while I had nothing.'
He said: 'Then a merchant came with goods and said to me,
He said: 'And he offered me his goods, so I would give him something for which he had not sold them. I said to him,
He said: 'How will I benefit from that?' I said to him, 'God be to you for that.'
He said, 'Take an equivalent from it.' So I took it, marked it, and severe cold came, so I sold the goods on the same day and paid him the price and took the surplus.
So I continued taking an equivalent, selling it, taking the surplus, and returning the principal to him, until I rode mounts, bought slaves, and built houses.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and practice for overcoming financial distress and gaining provision?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter of the 'Prayer of the Distressed' (Salat al-Mudtir) illustrates the practical application of tawakkul through a specific ritual of prayer and dhikr, emphasizing that divine provision (rizq) is contingent upon effort and spiritual reliance. The Imam’s instruction to sweep the shop signifies preparing the vessel for blessing, while the supplication explicitly rejects self-sufficiency in favor of God’s power, a core Shia theological concept. The narrative demonstrates how consistent adherence to this spiritual and commercial discipline transformed temporary distress into lasting prosperity, validating the efficacy of prescribed supplications in worldly affairs.
